the-modern-ai-agent-2023.name: The modern AI agent
the-modern-ai-agent-2023.definition: A software system built on a large language model that perceives its environment, reasons over open-ended tasks, and acts through tools in a loop.
the-modern-ai-agent-2023.bottleneck: Before the modern AI agent, machines could not perceive, reason over, and act on open-ended tasks in a loop, because no model could flexibly convert between language, perception and action, and there was no practical way to train or steer such a model.
the-modern-ai-agent-2023.leap: Instruction-following LLMs wrapped in a reason-act loop with tool use (2022-23: ChatGPT, ReAct, function calling) turned a text completer into a general task executor — a capability jump, not an incremental accuracy gain.
the-modern-ai-agent-2023.prior_state: Chatbots and task-specific ML systems: models could complete text or classify inputs, but could not follow open-ended instructions reliably, use external tools, or chain reasoning and action toward a goal.

in-context-learning-2020.name: In-context learning
in-context-learning-2020.definition: Few-shot conditioning phenomenon documented with GPT-3 (2020): models perform new tasks from examples in the prompt alone.
in-context-learning-2020.bottleneck: Before in-context learning, adapting a model to a new task required gradient updates and labeled datasets, because behavior could not be specified at inference time.
in-context-learning-2020.leap: GPT-3 (2020) demonstrated that a frozen model performs new tasks from examples and instructions in its prompt - behavior programmed in natural language at inference time.
in-context-learning-2020.prior_state: Fine-tuning per task; zero-shot transfer limited to narrow formats.

react-2022.name: ReAct
react-2022.definition: Prompting framework (Yao et al., 2022) interleaving reasoning traces with environment actions; beat imitation/RL baselines by 34% on ALFWorld and 10% on WebShop.
react-2022.bottleneck: Before ReAct, a language model could reason or act but not interleave the two, because reasoning traces were disconnected from environment feedback.
react-2022.leap: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022) interleaved thought, action, and observation; with 1-2 exemplars it beat imitation/RL baselines by 34 points on ALFWorld and 10 on WebShop.
react-2022.prior_state: CoT reasoned blind (hallucination, error propagation); act-only policies could not plan or recover.

transformer-architecture-2017.name: Transformer architecture
transformer-architecture-2017.definition: Sequence architecture based entirely on self-attention (Vaswani et al., 2017), replacing recurrence and enabling large-scale parallel training.
transformer-architecture-2017.bottleneck: Before the Transformer, sequence models could not train in parallel over long contexts, because recurrence forced sequential computation and vanishing information flow.
transformer-architecture-2017.leap: 'Attention Is All You Need' (2017) reached state-of-the-art translation in a fraction of prior training time and became the substrate of every frontier model that followed.
transformer-architecture-2017.prior_state: LSTM/GRU encoder-decoders with attention add-ons; slow sequential training and limited context.

large-scale-pretraining-gpt-3-2020.name: Large-scale pretraining (GPT-3)
large-scale-pretraining-gpt-3-2020.definition: Training very large autoregressive language models on web-scale text; GPT-3 (175B) showed few-shot in-context task performance without fine-tuning.
large-scale-pretraining-gpt-3-2020.bottleneck: Before GPT-3, a single model could not perform new tasks without gradient updates, because pretraining had never been scaled to the point where few-shot conditioning worked.
large-scale-pretraining-gpt-3-2020.leap: GPT-3 (175B, 2020) showed few-shot in-context task performance rivaling fine-tuned systems - one model, programmed by examples, replacing per-task training.
large-scale-pretraining-gpt-3-2020.prior_state: BERT-era practice: pretrain, then fine-tune a separate model per task.

reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedba.name: Reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF)
reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedba.definition: Training recipe that fine-tunes a language model with a reward model learned from human preference rankings, aligning outputs with judged helpfulness.
reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedba.bottleneck: Before RLHF, deployed language models could not be steered to follow human intent reliably, because pretraining optimizes text completion, not judged helpfulness.
reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedba.leap: RLHF fine-tuning (InstructGPT, 2022) made a 1.3B model preferred over the 175B GPT-3 - a discontinuous jump in instruction-following at fixed scale.
reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedba.prior_state: LLMs could be prompted or demonstration-tuned, but outputs were often unhelpful, evasive, or toxic; no deployed model reliably followed open-ended instructions.

hosted-llm-apis-openai-api-2020.name: Hosted LLM APIs (OpenAI API)
hosted-llm-apis-openai-api-2020.definition: Commercial API access to GPT-3 (June 2020 beta) and successors; models as a metered cloud service.
hosted-llm-apis-openai-api-2020.bottleneck: Before hosted LLM APIs, using a frontier model required training or hosting it yourself, because no one sold metered access to a general model.
hosted-llm-apis-openai-api-2020.leap: The OpenAI API (June 2020) made GPT-3 a metered cloud service; by 2023 the agent ecosystem ran overwhelmingly on hosted frontier APIs.
hosted-llm-apis-openai-api-2020.prior_state: Downloadable checkpoints for small models; in-house serving for large ones.

chain-of-thought-prompting-2022.name: Chain-of-thought prompting
chain-of-thought-prompting-2022.definition: Prompting method (Wei et al., 2022) in which exemplars with intermediate reasoning steps elicit step-by-step reasoning; PaLM 540B with 8 exemplars set GSM8K state of the art.
chain-of-thought-prompting-2022.bottleneck: Before chain-of-thought, large models could not do multi-step reasoning in the open, because they had to answer in one forward leap from question to answer.
chain-of-thought-prompting-2022.leap: CoT prompting (Wei et al., 2022): 8 exemplars made PaLM 540B set GSM8K state of the art (58.1%), surpassing fine-tuned GPT-3 with a verifier - reasoning as an elicitable behavior.
chain-of-thought-prompting-2022.prior_state: Standard prompting gave flat scaling on reasoning tasks; scratchpad methods existed only as trained-from-scratch curiosities.

chatgpt-2022.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt-2022.definition: OpenAI's November 2022 product: an RLHF-tuned GPT-3.5 model in a chat interface; fastest-adopted consumer application of its time.
chatgpt-2022.bottleneck: Before ChatGPT, the public and builders could not interact with an aligned LLM as a general assistant, because aligned models existed only as research demos and APIs for specialists.
chatgpt-2022.leap: ChatGPT (Nov 30, 2022) put an RLHF-tuned model in a chat product reaching 100M users in two months - the fastest-adopted application to that date - and became the surface agent frameworks wrapped.
chatgpt-2022.prior_state: GPT-3 playground/API for developers; chatbots with narrow skills for consumers.

codex-code-generation-model-2021.name: Codex code generation model
codex-code-generation-model-2021.definition: GPT model fine-tuned on public code (OpenAI, 2021) powering Copilot; showed LLMs could produce working programs from natural language.
codex-code-generation-model-2021.bottleneck: Before Codex, a machine could not turn a natural-language specification into working code at useful reliability, because code models had never been trained at GPT scale on public repositories.
codex-code-generation-model-2021.leap: Codex (2021) solved 28.8% of HumanEval problems zero-shot (vs 0% for GPT-3), and powered Copilot - code as a general actuation channel for LLMs.
codex-code-generation-model-2021.prior_state: Program synthesis research systems and autocomplete over tokens, neither usable as a general tool.

instruction-tuning-flan-2021.name: Instruction tuning (FLAN)
instruction-tuning-flan-2021.definition: Fine-tuning language models on mixtures of tasks phrased as instructions, yielding zero-shot task following (FLAN, T0).
instruction-tuning-flan-2021.bottleneck: Before instruction tuning, language models could not perform unseen tasks from a plain-language specification, because they had only ever been trained to continue text.
instruction-tuning-flan-2021.leap: FLAN (2021) showed fine-tuning on 60+ instruction-phrased tasks yields large zero-shot gains on unseen tasks - task following as a trainable, general capability.
instruction-tuning-flan-2021.prior_state: Zero-shot task performance required per-task fine-tuning or careful few-shot prompt craft.

retrieval-augmented-generation-2020.name: Retrieval-augmented generation
retrieval-augmented-generation-2020.definition: Architecture coupling a parametric language model with a non-parametric retrieval index over external documents (Lewis et al., 2020).
retrieval-augmented-generation-2020.bottleneck: Before RAG, a language model's knowledge was frozen at training time, because generation had no channel to external, updatable memory.
retrieval-augmented-generation-2020.leap: RAG (Lewis et al., 2020) coupled a retriever to a generator and beat closed-book models on open-domain QA, establishing retrieval as a model component.
retrieval-augmented-generation-2020.prior_state: Closed-book LMs answering from weights; separate IR pipelines feeding rigid templates.

instructgpt-2022.name: InstructGPT
instructgpt-2022.definition: OpenAI's GPT-3 fine-tuned with supervised demonstrations plus RLHF; labelers preferred its outputs to a 100x larger base model.
instructgpt-2022.bottleneck: Before InstructGPT, no one had shown a language model could be made to follow instructions better by training on human judgments, because alignment had not been operationalized as a training pipeline.
instructgpt-2022.leap: InstructGPT (Mar 2022) was the first system whose smaller aligned model beat its 100x larger base model on human preference - the steering discontinuity, demonstrated.
instructgpt-2022.prior_state: GPT-3 deployments relied on prompt engineering; outputs frequently ignored the instruction's intent.

candidate.key_mechanism: A sequence model reads labeled examples and predicts for queries using attention to history.
candidate.name: SNAIL
candidate.problem_solved: Meta-learned with temporal convolutions and attention over past experience.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Strong few-shot results with a model-based meta-learner.

candidate.key_mechanism: Move the initialization toward weights obtained after training on a sampled task.
candidate.name: Reptile
candidate.problem_solved: Simplified first-order meta-learning for fast adaptation.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Widely used simple meta-learning baseline.

aliases: Optimization as a Model for Few-Shot Learning

candidate.name: LSTM meta-learner
candidate.problem_solved: Learned an optimizer that adapts a learner to few-shot tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Optimization-based meta-learning milestone.

candidate.name: Learning to learn by gradient descent

candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded learned-optimizer research.

candidate.scale_or_impact: Model-based meta-learning milestone for one-shot tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: A meta network produces fast weights for a base learner conditioned on support examples.
candidate.name: Meta Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Adapted rapidly by generating fast weights from task context.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Fast-weight meta-learning milestone.

candidate.key_mechanism: Context points are encoded and aggregated into a representation conditioning the decoder.
candidate.name: Conditional Neural Processes
candidate.problem_solved: Predicted functions from a few context points in one forward pass.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded the neural-process family of conditional meta-learning.

candidate.key_mechanism: An RNN policy's hidden state carries experience across episodes of a task, implementing learning in activations.
candidate.lineage: Conceptual ancestor of in-context reinforcement learning.
candidate.name: RL^2
candidate.problem_solved: Learned a reinforcement-learning algorithm itself inside a recurrent policy.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early demonstration of learning-in-activations meta-RL.

candidate.key_mechanism: An LSTM agent trained across task distributions develops internal learning behavior.
candidate.name: Learning to reinforcement learn
candidate.problem_solved: Showed recurrent networks can implement a learning algorithm in their dynamics.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Parallel meta-RL milestone to RL^2.

candidate.key_mechanism: A Bayesian model transfers priors from previously learned categories to a new one.
candidate.lineage: Origin of the few-shot problem formulation.
candidate.name: One-shot learning of object categories
candidate.problem_solved: Learned a visual category from one or a few images using prior knowledge.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Stated the few-shot learning problem for modern ML.

aliases: Human-level concept learning through probabilistic program induction
candidate.key_mechanism: Probabilistic programs compose primitives into concepts, inferred by Bayesian sampling.
candidate.name: Bayesian program learning
candidate.problem_solved: Matched human one-shot concept learning on handwritten characters.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Set the human-level one-shot benchmark (Omniglot).

candidate.key_mechanism: 1,623 characters from 50 alphabets, 20 examples each, collected via Mechanical Turk.
candidate.name: Omniglot
candidate.problem_solved: Provided a standard one-shot classification benchmark of handwritten characters.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The standard few-shot benchmark of the 2010s.

candidate.key_mechanism: 100 ImageNet classes with 600 images each, split for meta-training and meta-testing.
candidate.name: miniImageNet
candidate.problem_solved: Gave few-shot image classification a standard episodic benchmark.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard benchmark for meta-learning methods.

candidate.key_mechanism: A research program and edited volume defining inductive transfer across task families.
candidate.name: Learning to learn (Thrun and Pratt)
candidate.problem_solved: Formalized learning-to-learn as improving at tasks with experience across tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Named the meta-learning field.

candidate.key_mechanism: Self-referential weight matrices learn to change their own update rules.
candidate.name: Self-referential meta-learning
candidate.problem_solved: Proposed networks that modify their own learning algorithm.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early theoretical statement of meta-learning.

aliases: Baxter model of inductive bias learning
candidate.key_mechanism: Sample-complexity bounds for learning a hypothesis-space family from task samples.
candidate.lineage: Theory root of transfer across tasks.
candidate.name: Inductive bias learning
candidate.problem_solved: Gave a theoretical model of learning an inductive bias from many tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Theory foundation for multi-task and meta-learning.

aliases: Using Fast Weights to Attend to the Recent Past
candidate.key_mechanism: A slow network programs fast weights that temporarily store recent associations.
candidate.name: Fast weights
candidate.problem_solved: Gave networks a rapidly changing memory for recent context.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Linked attention to fast-weight memory; later used to theorize ICL.

candidate.key_mechanism: A slow net generates weight changes for a fast net, storing sequences in weights.
candidate.lineage: Deep mechanism ancestor of attention/ICL theory.
candidate.name: Fast weight programmers
candidate.problem_solved: Let one network program another network's weights from context.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Anticipated attention and in-context weight-space learning.

candidate.key_mechanism: A small hypernetwork outputs the weights of a larger main network.
candidate.name: Hypernetworks
candidate.problem_solved: Generated one network's weights with another network conditioned on context.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Established weight-generation as a conditioning mechanism.

candidate.key_mechanism: A controller uses attention-like read/write heads over a memory matrix.
candidate.name: Neural Turing Machines
candidate.problem_solved: Gave neural networks a differentiable external memory they could read and write.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded differentiable-memory architectures.

candidate.key_mechanism: Inputs are written to memory slots; a controller reads relevant slots to answer.
candidate.name: Memory Networks
candidate.problem_solved: Let models reason over an explicit memory of facts at inference time.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early conditioning-on-context architecture for QA.

aliases: Hybrid computing using a neural network with dynamic external memory
candidate.key_mechanism: Content and temporal-link addressing over a memory matrix with allocation tracking.
candidate.name: Differentiable Neural Computer
candidate.problem_solved: Learned algorithmic reasoning over a dynamic external memory.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Extended NTMs to graph-like reasoning tasks.

candidate.key_mechanism: A differentiable memory module stores key-value pairs updated by a life-long memory learner.
candidate.name: Learning to remember rare events
candidate.problem_solved: Remembered rare examples after a single exposure for one-shot classification.
candidate.scale_or_impact: One-shot memory milestone.

candidate.key_mechanism: A recurrent controller calls learned sub-programs with arguments over an environment.
candidate.name: Neural Programmer-Interpreters
candidate.problem_solved: Learned reusable programs from execution traces.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Program-induction milestone.

candidate.key_mechanism: A domain-specific language plus version-space search finds programs matching the examples.
candidate.name: Programming by example (FlashFill)
candidate.problem_solved: Synthesized string-transformation programs from a few input-output examples.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Shipped in Excel 2013; specification-by-example at mass scale.

candidate.key_mechanism: A value network takes state and goal as inputs, enabling zero-shot goal transfer.
candidate.name: Universal value function approximators
candidate.problem_solved: Generalized value functions across goals so policies condition on goals.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Founded goal-conditioned value learning.

candidate.key_mechanism: A Fisher-information penalty protects weights important to earlier tasks.
candidate.lineage: Continual-learning fix for the paradigm ICL sidesteps.
candidate.name: Elastic weight consolidation
candidate.problem_solved: Reduced catastrophic forgetting when learning sequential tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard continual-learning baseline.

candidate.key_mechanism: Experiments and analysis showing distributed representations overwrite prior tasks.
candidate.lineage: Negative-space problem for the fine-tuning paradigm.
candidate.name: Catastrophic interference
candidate.problem_solved: Documented that sequential gradient training erases earlier learning.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Named the forgetting problem motivating adaptation research.

aliases: Fast mapping in early word learning
candidate.key_mechanism: Developmental experiments on one-shot word learning by exclusion.
candidate.name: Fast mapping
candidate.problem_solved: Showed children form partial word meanings from a single exposure.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Cognitive origin of the one-shot learning concept.

candidate.key_mechanism: Attribute classifiers mediate between images and unseen class labels.
candidate.name: Zero-shot learning
candidate.problem_solved: Classified unseen classes described by semantic attributes.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Defined zero-shot recognition in vision.

aliases: Google's Multilingual Neural Machine Translation System
candidate.key_mechanism: A single NMT model with a target-language token transfers across pairs zero-shot.
candidate.name: Multilingual zero-shot translation
candidate.problem_solved: Translated between language pairs never seen together in training.
candidate.scale_or_impact: First large-scale zero-shot transfer phenomenon in production NNs.

candidate.key_mechanism: A shared leaderboard of sentence and sentence-pair tasks.
candidate.lineage: Measurement of the paradigm ICL displaced.
candidate.name: GLUE
candidate.problem_solved: Measured general language understanding across nine tasks in one benchmark.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The scoreboard of the fine-tune era.

candidate.key_mechanism: Ten more difficult language-understanding tasks with a public leaderboard.
candidate.name: SuperGLUE
candidate.problem_solved: Replaced GLUE with harder tasks after models saturated it.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Scoreboard for BERT-era transfer.

candidate.key_mechanism: Questions whose answers are spans in Wikipedia paragraphs, crowdsourced.
candidate.name: SQuAD
candidate.problem_solved: Gave reading comprehension a 100k-question benchmark.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Drove the transfer-era QA race.

candidate.key_mechanism: Iteratively merge frequent character pairs into a subword vocabulary.
candidate.lineage: Tokenization component of the GPT line.
candidate.name: Byte pair encoding
candidate.problem_solved: Handled open vocabularies by segmenting words into frequent subwords.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard tokenization for GPT-class models.

aliases: Regularizing and Optimizing LSTM Language Models
candidate.key_mechanism: Weight-dropped LSTM with variational dropout and averaged SGD.
candidate.name: AWD-LSTM
candidate.problem_solved: Made LSTM language models train to much lower perplexity with strong regularization.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The base model ULMFiT transferred.

aliases: Deep contextualized word representations from MT
candidate.key_mechanism: A two-layer LSTM MT encoder's outputs serve as contextual word vectors.
candidate.name: CoVe
candidate.problem_solved: Transferred representations from machine translation encoders to other tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early pretrained-representation transfer result.

candidate.key_mechanism: An encoder-decoder is trained to predict surrounding sentences.
candidate.name: Skip-thought vectors
candidate.problem_solved: Learned generic sentence representations without labels.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early unsupervised sentence-representation milestone.

candidate.key_mechanism: Transformer or deep-averaging encoders trained on multi-task data.
candidate.name: Universal Sentence Encoder
candidate.problem_solved: Provided off-the-shelf sentence embeddings for transfer tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Widely used transfer embeddings.

candidate.key_mechanism: Siamese fine-tuning of BERT with pooling for similarity tasks.
candidate.name: Sentence-BERT
candidate.problem_solved: Made BERT produce usable sentence embeddings efficiently.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard sentence-embedding recipe.

candidate.key_mechanism: Pretrain an LSTM as a language model or autoencoder, then fine-tune on labeled data.
candidate.name: Semi-supervised sequence learning
candidate.problem_solved: Showed unsupervised pre-training of sequence models improves supervised tasks.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Early modern statement of the pretrain-fine-tune recipe.

aliases: Deep Learning Scaling is Predictable, Empirically
candidate.key_mechanism: Empirical fits of learning curves across translation, LM, and recognition tasks.
candidate.name: Empirical scaling trends (Hestness et al.)
candidate.problem_solved: Showed deep-learning performance follows predictable power laws with data and model size.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Evidence base for the scale-up strategy behind GPT-2/GPT-3.

candidate.key_mechanism: Large LSTM LMs with character-input and sampling corrections at 1B-word scale.
candidate.name: Exploring the limits of language modeling
candidate.problem_solved: Mapped what large-scale LSTM language models could achieve on a billion-word corpus.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Pre-Transformer large-LM reference point.

member_names: Exploring the limits of language modeling

candidate.lineage: Sequence-model substrate displaced by the Transformer.
candidate.name: LSTM
candidate.problem_solved: Let recurrent networks learn long-range dependencies without vanishing gradients.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Default sequence model for two decades.

candidate.key_mechanism: Entropy and n-gram statistics measure the predictability of symbol sequences.
candidate.name: Shannon information theory
candidate.problem_solved: Quantified information and prediction, founding statistical language modeling.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Foundation of information theory and LM evaluation.

candidate.key_mechanism: Conditional probabilities over word histories with smoothing and backoff.
candidate.name: N-gram language models
candidate.problem_solved: Predicted words from fixed-order Markov statistics for speech recognition.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard LM technology for three decades.

candidate.key_mechanism: GPT-2 conditioned on the story so far generates continuations for arbitrary player inputs.
candidate.lineage: Application of GPT-2 conditioning, downstream of it.
candidate.name: AI Dungeon
candidate.problem_solved: Let players steer open-ended stories by free-text actions in a GPT-2 world.
candidate.scale_or_impact: First mass-audience experience of prompt-conditioned generation.

candidate.key_mechanism: 8M web pages scraped from outbound Reddit links, curated for quality.
candidate.name: WebText
candidate.problem_solved: Provided diverse web text for training a general language model.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The training corpus behind GPT-2's zero-shot results.

candidate.key_mechanism: A public crawl archive of billions of web pages, updated monthly.
candidate.lineage: Data substrate of the LM era.
candidate.name: Common Crawl
candidate.problem_solved: Made petabyte-scale web text available for research.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Substrate corpus for most large LMs including GPT-3.

candidate.key_mechanism: 11k unpublished books scraped from Smashwords across genres.
candidate.name: BookCorpus
candidate.problem_solved: Provided long-form book text for training sentence and language models.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Training data for GPT-1 and BERT.

candidate.key_mechanism: 103M tokens from 28k verified-good Wikipedia articles.
candidate.name: WikiText-103
candidate.problem_solved: Gave language modeling a long-context Wikipedia benchmark corpus.
candidate.scale_or_impact: ULMFiT's pretraining corpus and a standard LM benchmark.

candidate.key_mechanism: One billion words of news text with a fixed train/test split.
candidate.name: One Billion Word Benchmark
candidate.problem_solved: Standardized large-scale statistical language modeling evaluation.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The benchmark of the large-LSTM LM era.

candidate.key_mechanism: One million words of Wall Street Journal text with POS tags and parse trees.
candidate.name: Penn Treebank
candidate.problem_solved: Provided parsed, tagged text that anchored LM and parsing research.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Standard LM testbed for two decades.

candidate.key_mechanism: A C-based platform exposing GPU thread hierarchies to developers.
candidate.lineage: Infrastructure under all large LM training.
candidate.name: CUDA
candidate.problem_solved: Made GPUs programmable for general-purpose parallel computing.
candidate.scale_or_impact: The compute substrate of the deep-learning era.

candidate.key_mechanism: Dataflow graphs executed on CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs with automatic differentiation.
candidate.lineage: Framework substrate of the pretraining era.
candidate.name: TensorFlow
candidate.problem_solved: Standardized building and training large neural networks across hardware.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Dominant research framework of the late 2010s.

candidate.key_mechanism: Dynamic computation graphs with autograd over GPU tensors.
candidate.lineage: Framework substrate of the pretraining era.
candidate.name: PyTorch
candidate.problem_solved: Made neural-network research programmable in imperative Python with GPU tensors.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Became the dominant research framework by 2019.

candidate.key_mechanism: Hebbian traces modulated by learned coefficients, trained by gradient descent.
candidate.name: Differentiable plasticity
candidate.problem_solved: Learned per-connection plasticity rules for fast within-lifetime adaptation.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Fast-adaptation mechanism research line.

candidate.key_mechanism: Per-parameter learned step sizes applied in inner-loop updates across tasks.
candidate.name: Meta-SGD
candidate.problem_solved: Meta-learned learning rates and update directions, not just initializations.
candidate.scale_or_impact: Optimization-based meta-learning variant.
